title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Below-Threshold Write-Off of Outpatient-Surgery Small Items
content:
**Denials desk note.** On a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim in denied status for an Outpatient Surgery Account, this rule takes the small items that pass the small-item test off the claim as one write-off entry with the write-off reason BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD, carrying the claim's current denial reason code; any other claim gets nothing here.

The Outpatient Surgery Account is the patient class of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) bills.

**What the write-off amount replaces.** For the small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list that pass the small-item test on a claim closed under this rule, and only for them, the amount written off below the appeal threshold is the surgery small-item value rather than their charges; take-home convenience items, the services closed on the member's decision, small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list, self-administered drugs and the services closed on the patient's external-review decision are written off under their own rules, and every other denied amount is written off in full by the hospital, never billed to the patient, when its route ends in a write-off: timely filing expired (no timely-filing proof), no authorization obtained (no authorization, notification, emergency exemption or retro authorization), non-covered with no waiver (no advance waiver on file), appeals exhausted (the last available level upheld the denial), or below the appeal threshold (a denied amount at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount that is not worth appealing).

**What stays on the claim.** The small-item charges above the surgery small-item value stay on the claim as the agreement's contractual remainder, which Riverbend's month-end contractual close posts on the last calendar day of the month.

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace Exchange Plan Claim, denied status, Outpatient Surgery Account | one below-threshold write-off entry for the passing small items |
| any other claim | nothing under this rule |

## Booking the write-off: `write_off_surgery_small_items_d7ad9b50`
**Capability.** Writes off, on one denied insurance claim, the value of small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list that are too small to carry into any further appeal: one write-off entry with the write-off reason BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD and the claim's current denial reason code, dated today, lowering the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. The patient is never billed for it; the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `write_off_surgery_small_items_d7ad9b50` and then calls it.

**Parameters**
- `claim_id` — the reference number of the insurance claim whose small items are written off, as shown by the claim lookup for the patient (identifier).
- `amount_usd` — the value being written off: USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent by the caller; posted exactly as given.

**Return.** A text receipt: "Write-off <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason BELOW_APPEAL_THRESHOLD, denial code <carc_code>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The entry reference identifies the new claim activity entry, the denial code is the claim's denial reason code copied onto the entry, and the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer (USD, 2 decimal places). The receipt appearing is the success signal.
